title: Make pending questions visible
account:
In this synthetic workflow exercise, a learner revisits the earlier draft handover as a teaching artifact, not as a clinical update. They group the note into reported observations, directly observed actions, working concerns, and pending questions. The owner history stays visible even though a diagnosis was never provided.

The group discusses making “unknown” a first-class value rather than leaving a blank space that a later reader could misinterpret. In the demonstration, the outcome field explicitly says unknown, and the pending-results question is carried forward with a source link. This change adds useful structure without rewriting the old shift entry.

No person is assigned a real task and no hospital policy is established. This is a demonstration of how a learner might preserve context for later review. Whether the proposed format is suitable for a particular hospital remains a local decision.

facts.text: Keep pending questions, their evidence, and unknown outcomes visible in the learning record.
No subsequent patient outcome is available in this exercise.

questions: Can a reader distinguish a completed action from an intended one?
conclusions: A proposed note format is recorded, not a new hospital policy.
